title: Three Vegan Korean Recipes: Kimchi Jigae, Japchae, and Tteokbokki
summary: In this Goodful tutorial, host Jasmine demonstrates three vegan-friendly Korean dishes: kimchi jigae (kimchi stew), japchae (stir-fried sweet potato noodles), and tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes). She adapts traditional flavors for vegan diets by using vegan-friendly kimchi, kelp-based umami instead of fish sauce, and tofu in the stew. The video walks through building each dish from base aromatics (onions, garlic), through sauce components (gochugaru, gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil), to final assembly and plating. Along the way, Jasmine offers practical tips on flavor balance (kimchi juice for tang, no alternative sweeteners), texture (blanching spinach to preserve color, soaking rice cakes to avoid soggy interiors), and kitchen workflow (one-pan methods for japchae, transferring to a larger pan when needed). The content blends cultural context with accessible substitutions, and notes a Lunar New Year association for the tteokbokki dish.

sections.title: Kimchi Jigae (Vegan Kimchi Stew)
sections.description: Jasmine makes a vegan kimchi jigae using vegan kimchi, garlic, onions, gochugaru, gochujang, kimchi juice, and kelp-based umami; tofu is added for texture, and the stew simmers to develop flavor before serving with rice.

sections.title: Japchae (Sweet Potato Noodle Stir-Fry)
sections.description: Japchae is prepared by blanching spinach, cooking sweet potato noodles, and combining with a quick one-pan mix of sautéed vegetables and marinated mushrooms, finished with a sesame-soy seasoning and sesame seeds.

sections.title: Tteokbokki (Spicy Rice Cakes) with Gocha Sauce
concepts: rice cakes soaking prior to cooking
finishing with green onions and sesame seeds
sections.description: Tteokbokki is prepared with a kelp-based broth and a gochujang-centered sauce, rice cakes pre-soaked to prevent sogginess, and optional ramen noodles folded in. The dish is finished with onions, cabbage, and sesame seeds, with a cultural note linking it to Lunar New Year.
